cases.name: Eleanor "Ellie" Louise Dietz
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Ellie’s favorite pastime was cuddling her stuffed animals, chasing bubbles, and spending time with her “Oma” Ursula Dietz. She loved to spend time outside following her older sister Natalie and doing all the things “Sissy” did. Ellie explored the world around her with a curious fervor, always sticking her hand in the toilet or examining things on the floor. She loved the songs “Head Shoulders Knees and Toes” and “The Itsy-Bitsy Spider.”

Ellie’s favorite people were her “Daddy” Patrick, “Mommy” Katherine, and the teachers at Child Care Network and the TSYS Learning Center. She always had a mischievous smile on her face and happily waved at anyone. She enjoyed blowing kisses to her adoring fans.

Ellie’s favorite food was steak (or any type of meat) and could eat half of a filet on her own. She would determine when the meal was over, regardless of whether other people were finished eating. Although she often enjoyed playing with her food more than eating it, more food ended up in her than on her.

Ellie’s favorite books were “But Not the Armadillo” and “Brown Bear, Brown Bear, What Do you See?” and wouldn’t settle down for bedtime unless each book was read at least two times."

cases.name: Ursula Dietz
cases.about:
Her obituary said, "Ursula “Uschi” Dietz was born to Heinz and Lieselotte Dietz on September 14th, 1958, in Homburg, Germany.

Ursula lived in Germany for most of her life. She studied Economics in Baden-Baden and held jobs in office administration, transcription, translation, and manufacturing. After marrying Gottfried Kaps, she often traveled to the United States, where she fell in love with the architecture and blue, sunny skies. She moved to Columbus, Georgia in 1992. She was a stay-at-home mom for many years, yet always found time to get involved in school events and activities, sports, and her children’s hobbies.

In 2005, Ursula became the owner of Bare Ware Pottery Studio, LLC. She always said it was her proudest achievement to become a business owner. Although she wasn’t the original owner, Bare Ware Pottery quickly became synonymous with Ursula and frequently had regulars spend most of their days at the studio. Anyone who visited Bare Ware Pottery Studio knew Ursula as the animated and active owner of the studio, often running circles around anyone there. She was always thorough and detailed, but calming enough to get a perfect baby footprint on any work of art.

Ursula’s favorite pastime was spending time with her grandchildren: Oliver, Natalie, and Eleanor. She enjoyed sitting by the pool in the spring and summer and bicycling in the fall and winter. She jumped at any opportunity to get out in the sunshine and fresh air.

Ursula’s favorite trip destination was Panama City Beach, with a detour to Chautauqua Vineyards and pick up a case of her two favorite wines, Sunset Red and Beachberry Breeze. She loved the beach and always wished to retire and buy a house in Florida. Ursula planned to retire in 2023."
